items.title: Avakian George — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He’d come over to Maro and Lisle’s house for dinner with his wife, that sort of thing.

ctx.x: God, look at all of the connections in my life. It’s incredible. Let’s get back to Buck Clayton and the jam session series. That was a terrifically exciting thing. We ended up doing them in terms of my going out in the studio and directing the musicians and just improvising the sequence of solos, because Buck said, “Look, you handle it. I’ve got enough in my hands working out the backgrounds ad lib and playing my own solos.” That was first real exploitation of long-playing records in the studio. It just hadn’t…

Our first two children were born in the summertime, and they were delighted that they could have their birthday parties at Auntie Maro’s house, because they had friends in the neighborhood, and it was more fun than New York. items.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011
items.q: And I remember George Avakian was surprised and we were all surprised that it sold as well as it did.

ctx.x: Wow. I’ll have to work on that for the Unitarian church that I play at. I’ll have to see if I can get that going. Back to paying dues. I don’t know if you would remember such an incident but would you remember the first time a check came to your house for one of Dave’s compositions? Like an ASCAP royalty or BMI or something like that?

No I don’t remember the first. Let me see. I remember a couple of things. I remember when Dave signed with Columbia he received an advance and of course there was royalties against the advance and I can remember being quite excited and surprised to see how fast he was able to reach that point to actually be receiving royalties, because he’d paid off the advance and was receiving royalties. Because “Jazz Goes to College” sold very well. And I remember George Avakian was surprised and we were all surprised that it…
And he would get slightly more money if he had his own compositions on the records too, wouldn’t he?
